clue.text: *Pleasing clues I do? I do!

indicators.note: the final exclamation 'do!' is an order to rework the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A solver delighted with a set of clues, cheering them on with 'I do! I do!'.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'do' is the anagram signal: CLUES, I, DO and I together shuffle into the answer. GOLDEN DELICIOUS is a variety of apple, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful to the taste or senses is pleasing.

clue.text: A piss-taker you are, texting totally lost lecturer

parts.note: in text-message shorthand 'you are' is written U R

indicators.note: something lost is taken away, so a letter goes from the phrase for 'totally'

parts.note: 'totally' can be expressed as 'in all'
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer, as on a learner plate

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a mocker whose texting has utterly baffled an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes one lecturer's letter from the phrase for 'totally'. 'Piss-taker' looks like a mocker but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A urinal is a fixture that receives, or literally takes, urine.

clue.text: Wants one to move out? Here you'd want to move in!

definitions.text: Here you'd want to move in!

indicators.note: a letter told to move out leaves the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: wants, as a noun, means desires
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An estate agent's quip: a tenant wants out, while a buyer would love to move in.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I (one) out of DESIRES. DES RES is estate-agent slang for a 'desirable residence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents' shorthand for an attractive property, the kind of home a buyer longs to occupy.

clue.text: *Fan admitting, in the end, bride's "busty" — at this?

indicators.note: a word admitting others lets them inside it

parts.note: a fan can mean a wing, as of a bird

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
DD is a large bra cup size, so it suggests 'busty'

explanation.surface: Someone fans a bride whose figure is on show, and asks at what event this happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals the container; 'in the end' takes the final letter of 'bride'. The definition 'at this?' asks where the busty bride appears. GOLDEN WEDDING is a fiftieth anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage ceremony is where you would find a bride.

clue.text: Ready for American weakling to describe principle

indicators.note: to describe here means to draw around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a runt is the weakling of a litter
'ready' is slang for cash; an American coin is a dime

explanation.surface: An American weakling ready to sketch out a basic idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe', in its geometrical sense of drawing a line around, is the container signal. 'Ready' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a basic principle or first element of a subject.

clue.text: *What's going on "Down Under"? Nothing

parts.note: hell is the place far down below
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Asking what is happening in Australia, to be told nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down Under' wants to be Australia; it is hell. A GOLDEN HELLO is a signing-on bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'hello, hello' is a way of asking what is happening here.

clue.text: *Will I get stick, on time, attending biblical class — without fail?

parts.note: re means about or on, as in a letter heading
RI is Religious Instruction, the school Bible lesson
ever can mean always, without fail

explanation.surface: A pupil worrying about punishment for being late to scripture lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get stick' suggests being told off; here it is fetching a thrown stick. RI, Religious Instruction, is a dated British school subject. GOLDEN RETRIEVER is a dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog bred to fetch, so it would be the one to bring back a thrown stick.

clue.text: *Top Christmasses after king is monarch

indicators.note: after places the Christmas piece second, behind the king

parts.note: R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas

explanation.surface: Seasonal festivities ranked below a king who reigns supreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' beheads the Christmas word, and 'after' puts it behind the king. GOLDEN RULE is a guiding principle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign or govern as a sovereign does.

clue.text: *Miracle — like floor-crossing Tory heading for the top?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going towards the top means the letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: a Conservative who crosses the floor of the House to Labour is now red

explanation.surface: Would a Conservative defecting while climbing to the top be a miracle?
explanation.walkthrough: Red is Labour's colour, so a defecting Tory is RED NOW, read upwards. GOLDEN WONDER is a British crisps brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonder is a marvel or extraordinary event.

clue.text: Quixote, say, engages single man

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Don Quixote; don is a Spanish title of respect
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: Don Quixote, the deluded knight, taking on a bachelor.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside DON. 'single man' reads as a bachelor, but 'single' supplies I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dion is a male first name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: *24D's got over cane

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: French d'or means 'of gold', what 24 down has

explanation.surface: Gold has been taken over by a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: D'OR, French for 'of gold', reversed. GOLDENROD is a yellow-flowered plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane is a stick, the same as a rod.

clue.text: *Bird's expressed encouragement to drink port

indicators.note: a drinker takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of encouragement
Rio de Janeiro is a port

explanation.surface: A bird cheered on to take a glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drink' signals the container. 'port' wants to be the wine; it is the Brazilian city. GOLDEN ORIOLE is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriole is a brightly coloured songbird.

clue.text: *Years in Copenhagen?

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the city's name

explanation.walkthrough: GOLDEN AGE is a period of prosperity.
explanation.definitionFit: A long period of time measured in years.

clue.text: *Contrasting ways to go after Joe's daughter

indicators.note: to go after something is to follow it, so these pieces come second

parts.note: GI Joe is an American soldier, a GI
right and left are opposite directions, R and L
right and left are opposite directions, R and L

explanation.surface: Different directions to follow after Joe's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L come after GI. GOLDEN GIRL is a star or favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, a young female.

clue.text: Function one spotted being indefinitely adjourned

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a die is marked with spots

explanation.surface: A meeting adjourned after a function where someone was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: SINE DIE is Latin for 'without a day', used of a meeting postponed with no date set.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term means postponed with no fixed date to resume.

clue.text: *Reach up at malfunctioning structure while going down

indicators.note: something malfunctioning works wrongly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone reaching up at a faulty canopy as they fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of REACH UP AT, rearranged. GOLDEN PARACHUTE is a generous severance payment for an executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy device that slows a fall through the air.

clue.text: *Celebration with humour over the third of the month

indicators.note: one piece placed over a letter covers it, taking its place

parts.note: June is a month
bile is one of the four humours of old medicine

explanation.surface: A party with jokes on the third day of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: BILE replaces N, the third letter of JUNE. 'humour' wants to mean comedy; it is the old medical sense. GOLDEN JUBILEE marks fifty years.
explanation.definitionFit: A jubilee is an anniversary celebration.

clue.text: Get behind Lindbergh thus?

explanation.surface: A pilot, Charles Lindbergh, urged to support someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lindbergh flew the Atlantic in the 'Spirit of St Louis', so he was in Spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage or rouse someone is to back them; Lindbergh flew aboard the aircraft called Spirit of St Louis.

clue.text: *We're a couple under 13 — Dicky and Lesley

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: 13 across is the answer to the clue 'Years'
Les is short for Lesley

explanation.surface: A couple under thirteen years old, named Dicky and Lesley.
explanation.walkthrough: An eagle in golf is a score two under par. 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram signal. GOLDEN EAGLE is a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, an eagle is a score of two strokes below par.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing acquires fine turning tool

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: turning around makes the letters run backwards

parts.note: a waster is a good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: A layabout gets hold of a fine lathe tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tool' suggests a lathe; 'turning' reverses WASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-bladed saw for cutting curves is a tool.

clue.text: What's 24D in excitement, indefinitely?

indicators.note: one piece is placed in another

parts.note: fever means excitement
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Asking what golden excitement means, for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. Gold is the heraldic tincture called 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Without end; permanently, without limit.

clue.text: Our deserts a problem for Holmes, clock out

indicators.note: something that deserts leaves, so these letters go

parts.note: The Sign of Four is a Sherlock Holmes case by Conan Doyle

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's puzzle about deserts before leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' looks like a noun; it is a verb, so OUR leaves SIGN OF FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish work, to end one's shift, is to sign off.

clue.text: *Charge too highly for woollen coat

explanation.surface: Overcharging someone for a wool garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is to swindle; a sheep's fleece is its woollen covering.

clue.text: *Holiday destination that's popular, and off Land's End

parts.note: Goa is a popular Indian holiday resort

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so these letters go

parts.note: land given as written

explanation.surface: A popular holiday spot off the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: AND is removed from LAND, leaving L. 'Land's End' looks like the Cornish headland; 'End' is the definition. GOLDEN GOAL decided some football matches.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or objective is what one ends up working towards.

clue.text: Happy news about antique

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: gen is slang for information, news
antique means old

explanation.surface: Glad tidings concerning an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. 'Happy' as in golden days, a time of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden can mean joyful or prosperous, as in golden days.

clue.text: *What's the matter, trains being held up? Sticky liquid

indicators.note: something held is contained inside another piece

parts.note: 'sup is slang for 'what's up?', what's the matter

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run backwards

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, trains

explanation.surface: Asking what's wrong when trains are delayed by something sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the railway abbreviation upwards in this down entry, and 'being held' puts it inside. 'held up' suggests delayed trains. GOLDEN SYRUP is a sweet syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick, sweet liquid that is sticky.

clue.text: Look round little boys room

parts.note: lo means look; that 'Look' also starts with the answer's letters is a coincidence
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Looking around a small boys' bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little boys room' suggests a child's bedroom; it is a euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'little boys' room' is a coy euphemism for a toilet.

clue.text: 50 not out, cutting extra boundary

indicators.note: a piece cutting another goes into it

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
L is the Roman numeral fifty
a batsman not out is still in

explanation.surface: A cricketer on fifty, not out, hitting an extra to the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' signals the container. 'Not out', 'extra' and 'boundary' are cricket terms in the surface, but the definition is the football byline.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline is the line at the end of a pitch, a boundary.

clue.text: *Looker of The Year

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: A beautiful person crowned as looker of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looker' suggests a beauty; it is the organ that looks. GOLDENEYE is a duck, and a Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is the organ for looking.

clue.text: Old actor of note so anticipates taking a little time

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa, so is followed by la
hr is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: An elderly performer expecting to take time over a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Bert Lahr was the Cowardly Lion in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Bert Lahr was a vaudeville and film performer of the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: The day after Jun 30, a woman appears

parts.note: 1 July is written JUL 1, with 1 as I

explanation.surface: A woman shows up on the first of July.
explanation.walkthrough: The day after 30 June is 1 July, written JUL I with a Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Julia is a female first name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Packing cases a pain during exams

indicators.note: one piece occurs within another

parts.note: tests are exams
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A worried student with a pain during examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals the container; 'a' is a link word, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Large wooden boxes for tea, used for packing in moves.
